A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MROT research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original MROT experiments on synthetic data, AdBench and Tennessee Eastman simulations, including benchmark results and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports PR-AUC results, a regression-model ablation and detailed Tennessee Eastman results by anomaly percentage.

M1.justification: V2 broadens the specified ground cost from a neighborhood-local supremum to a configurable finite penalty L and general neighborhoods, and explicitly selects full-row maxima for experiments. The OT, transportation-effort, CDF and regression pipeline remains. V1 already illustrates a high exclusion penalty, so the PDFs establish a specification refinement without establishing an implementation change or rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the Gaussian toy example, 47 real-world AdBench datasets, five NLP datasets and six Tennessee Eastman modes with varying anomaly percentages. V2's named NLP rows and expanded process description document retained coverage. V1's discussion of cross-domain detection did not include a corresponding reported experiment.

E2.justification: The corresponding AdBench and Tennessee Eastman comparisons retain their comparator sets, including classical detectors, diffusion methods and OT with the regularized Coulomb cost. OT and ROT denote the same comparator. Newly cited deep-learning methods are not added to the benchmark comparisons; regression variants are examined within an ablation.

E3.justification: V2 adds PR-AUC alongside ROC-AUC and introduces experimental configurations comparing XGBoost, SVR and nearest-neighbor regression. The sample cap, epsilon/k grids and Tennessee Eastman anomaly-percentage design remain. Its contradictory appendix timing descriptions do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun under different settings.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Figure 13 add a systematic regression-stage ablation across neighborhood sizes, extending substantially beyond v1's toy illustrations of XGBoost and SVR. Appendix Figure 14 also supplies anomaly-percentage-specific Tennessee Eastman behavior previously represented only through aggregates. The original epsilon/k sensitivity analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use plus/minus entries in the AdBench results and distribution plots. V2 extends this reporting style to additional results but adds no run counts, seed information, confidence-interval definitions or significance tests.

E6.justification: All 47 original ROC-AUC table rows remain identical, including the MROT and OT averages of 77.36 and 75.97. V2 adds dataset-level NLP ROC-AUC entries, a full PR-AUC table, regression-ablation results and Tennessee Eastman percentage curves. Newly reported real-world PR-AUC averages are 39.95 for MROT and 39.60 for OT.

T1.justification: New Section 3.3 introduces existence theorems and a continuity proof for a particular continuous cost, plus discrete existence and entropic-uniqueness arguments. V2 also adds a large-epsilon limiting derivation and a Gaussian Wasserstein interpretation of process features. These substantially extend v1's definitions and intuitive motivation, although edited formulas introduce errors such as p_i >= 1 in Equation 2.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a general-purpose OT-based anomaly detector, engineered exclusion costs, a generalizable anomaly score and strong real-world benchmark performance. The claimed novelty relative to previous OT-based detection is retained. V2's explicit reference to real-world benchmarks in the conclusion reflects qualifications already present in v1.

C2.justification: V2 explains large entropic penalties as reducing transportation effort to average cost, attributes weaker nearest-neighbor regression to overfitting, and suggests specific future remedies for scalability and high dimensionality. It also distinguishes theoretical and practical penalty choices. The central density-based explanation and principal empirical limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly supplies a code-repository link and substantial Tennessee Eastman documentation: operation-mode definitions, selected variables, fault-injection timing and explicit window statistics. These document existing experiments rather than establish new coverage. Reproducibility remains impaired by the appendix's 100-hour, three-minute account conflicting with the retained 600-hour, hourly account in Section 4.2.

R1.justification: V2 expands the deep-learning discussion with works including Pang, Ruff, Schlegl, Zenati and Akcay, and adds references supporting OT theory and possible computational remedies. Several domain-adaptation references disappear. These are targeted expansions; the main positioning against neighborhood detectors, repulsive OT and earlier OT-based anomaly detection remains.

P1.justification: V2 edits terminology and explanatory prose, makes the toy example unnumbered, inserts a theoretical-analysis subsection, expands Robustness into Ablations and separates the concluding limitations discussion. The author footnote also changes to equal contribution. Much of the original prose and the overall introduction-to-method-to-experiments structure remain.

P2.justification: V2 adds conceptual and empirical OT illustrations, redraws the cost comparison with two penalty choices, and expands benchmark summaries with PR-AUC panels. It also adds regression and anomaly-percentage plots, a PR-AUC table and process-description tables. Existing toy displays are split, expanded and rearranged, producing substantial visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the work easier to assess through explicit cost choices, existence and uniqueness analysis, PR-AUC reporting, a regression ablation and the previously missing Tennessee Eastman breakdown. The code link and implementation documentation also help. However, new mathematical errors, including p_i >= 1 in Equation 2, and contradictory simulation timing in Appendix A.2 weaken the gains in rigor and reproducibility. The net improvement is therefore limited.
